prompt: Stage 3-1, level 5, 52 gold, 80 HP. The shop shows a third copy of your 2-cost caster (2 gold; it would become a 2-star on the board) and a second copy of a 3-cost bruiser you hold on the bench (3 gold, a pair). Interest is 1 gold per 10 held, up to 5 at 50. What do you buy?

options.label: Buy the caster copy only: 52 becomes 50, still 5 interest, and the caster on the board becomes a 2-star
Buy the bruiser copy only: 52 becomes 49, a pair of a stronger unit
Buy both: 52 becomes 47, you get the 2-star and the pair

explanation:
The interest breakpoint is 50: 52 and 50 both earn 5 gold next round, 49 earns 4. So the caster copy is effectively free: 2 gold for a 2-star on a unit already on the board, and the interest is untouched. The bruiser copy costs 3 gold plus 1 gold of interest next round, for a pair you may never complete, and if you buy both you are at 47 and paying the same lost interest for a 2-star you could have had for 2.

This is the whole skill of sitting at 50: you do not stop buying, you check where the purchase lands. On or above a multiple of 10 it costs its price; below, it costs its price plus the interest you crossed. Buy the 2-star, keep 50, and if the bruiser pair is still there after 3-2's income, buy it then from above 50. Buying neither leaves a 2-star on the screen for no reason: the copy is gone when the shop refreshes.
principle: Check where a buy lands: at 50 it costs its price, at 49 it costs its price plus a gold every round until you climb back.
commonMistake: Treating every cheap buy as the same cost, and dropping from 52 to 47 for two units when one of them was free and the other was not.
hint: Do the subtraction for each option and see which ones stay on or above 50. Then ask which purchase goes on the board this round.
